To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
flight delays in the US air system have a significant impact on both airfare and flight frequencies.

flight delays are associated with both higher fare and higher frequency of service, that the magnitude of these impacts varies by airline, by airport, and by season, and that proportionate delay reduction across the entire system would lead to fare reductions in the order of $0.8 billion annually.
airlines tend to increase fare and frequency in response to flight delays.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of flight delay on airfare and frequency in a competitive market environment.
the economic impact of flight delay in the US air transport industry and provides insights for both airline management and policy makers.
understanding the relationship between flight delay, airfare and flight frequencies, which are important for both the airline industry and air travelers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the US air transportation is not a competitive market and the market is far from being a perfectly competitive one.
delay cost is passed on to the passenger through higher fares.
delay reduction is beneficial to the air transportation system, and that delay reduction is not necessarily associated with lower airfares.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
flight delay cost can be reduced by 10%, and airfare can be reduced by about 0.2%.
delay reduction can be a cost-effective way to improve the efficiency of the air transportation system, but the benefit of delay reduction can vary significantly by airport and time of day.
delay has a negative impact on airfare but a positive effect on flight frequency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the US air transportation is not a competitive market.
the current air transportation system is highly inefficient in terms of delay and its impact on airfare.
the US airline industry can benefit from more efficient airport management, which would result in lower airfare and more frequent flights.
